headline: No meaningful interaction risk: both profiles are documentation-only, non-runnable, and expose no shared I/O or write surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dagster and python-cheatsheet are both non-runnable documentation-only profiles with no clipboard, stdin/stdout, files, MCP, or browser surfaces. There is no shared communication channel for one to inject instructions into the other, so the pathway is provably blocked.
conditions: IF either profile gains a shared clipboard, stdin/stdout, or file bridge, re-evaluate injection risk.
mitigations: Keep both agents documentation-only.
Do not connect them through copy-paste automation.
Avoid adding shared filesystem mounts.
requires-engineering: If future orchestration adds a bridge, add provenance tagging and filtering.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Neither agent reads files, writes files, or sends network traffic by default, and both profiles touch no data classes. With no shared workspace or outbound transport, there is no plausible leakage path between dagster and python-cheatsheet.
conditions: IF either agent is granted filesystem access or network egress, reassess leakage risk.
mitigations: Keep network egress disabled.
Keep filesystem access disabled.
Do not place sensitive files in a shared workspace.
requires-engineering: Add explicit data-flow controls before enabling any I/O.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both profiles have execute_shell, write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and subprocess spawning disabled, and python-cheatsheet also cannot support multiple instances. Without overlapping write capabilities or mutable shared resources, there is no capability conflict between the pair.
conditions: IF either agent is later given write access to the same mutable resource, re-evaluate conflict risk.
mitigations: Keep write permissions disabled.
Avoid shared mutable repositories.
Do not co-schedule them against the same stateful target.
requires-engineering: Add locking if shared mutable resources are introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dagster is an orchestrator profile, but here it is non-runnable and has no I/O surfaces; python-cheatsheet is documentation-only. Since neither agent can produce actionable outputs that the other would consume as authoritative, there is no cascading-error pathway in this pair.
conditions: IF either agent begins emitting machine-actionable instructions into an automated pipeline, reassess cascading error risk.
mitigations: Keep outputs human-reviewed.
Do not wire one agent directly into the other's action path.
Avoid automated execution of generated text.
requires-engineering: Add verification gates before any downstream action-taking.

E_compliance.rationale: No data classes are touched by either profile, and neither profile requests secrets, OAuth scopes, or elevated privileges. With no identifiable regulated data flow, there is no compliance mismatch to assess between dagster and python-cheatsheet.
conditions: IF regulated data is later routed through either profile, reassess residency and retention requirements.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both profiles.
Document any future data-class handling.
Review residency and retention before enabling storage.
requires-engineering: Add compliance controls if regulated data is introduced.
